public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in AI & Compute

data.narrative:
Core Automation, a stealth-stage AI & Software company founded by Gerald Depew and Daniel C. Rozok, is targeting a Series funding round of $500M–$1B at a post-money valuation of $4–5B+. The relevant comp universe consists of one public company (Palantir, ticker PLTR) and eight private peers, including Figure AI, Scale AI, Reflection AI, and Applied Intuition.

Peer-median valuation analysis was not applicable in this case. The broader AI & Software sector contains 12 comparable companies, but none met the narrow filtering criteria for stage alignment, adjacent-stage proximity, or similar valuation tier—requiring a minimum of three datapoints per method. Applying an all-sector median would introduce substantial noise and misalignment given the heterogeneity of AI & Software business models and maturity levels at different fundraising stages. This methodological constraint significantly limits triangulation capacity at the current stage of company maturity.

The stated target valuation of $4–5B+ reflects the founders' ask and the market's current appetite for frontier AI infrastructure. Without sufficient same-stage or tier-matched comparables to anchor a quantitative cross-check, key uncertainties remain around revenue trajectory, unit economics, and competitive differentiation relative to the named peer set. A more robust valuation will require either advancement to a later stage with clearer metrics or identification of additional stealth-stage AI infrastructure companies with disclosed or inferred valuations.
